 1   INTRODUCTION
 2   Q.   Please state your name, occupation and business address.

 3   A.   My name is Daren K. Zigich. I am a Licensed Professional Engineer employed by the New

 4        Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“NMPRC” or “Commission”) in the Utility

 5        Division. My business address is P.O. Box 1269, Santa Fe, NM 87504.

 6

 7   Q.   Have you previously testified in this case?

 8   A.   Yes, I provided written direct testimony on May 1, 2026.

 9

10   Q.   Have you prepared any exhibits?

11   A.   No.


12   BACKGROUND
13   Q.   What is the purpose of your testimony?

14   A.   The purpose of my testimony is to relay a portion of Staff’s opposition and non-opposition

15        to the Comprehensive Stipulation reached by SPS and various intervenors in this case.

16

17   Q.   What specific parts of the Stipulation are you addressing?

18   A.   My testimony focuses on stipulated condition 1.3 while also providing additional

19        comments on condition 1.11, which is more thoroughly covered by Staff witnesses Blank

20        and Rilkoff. Additionally, my testimony will highlight four specific stipulated conditions

21        that are not opposed by Staff. As highlighted in the previously filed Exhibit A to Staff’s

22        Statement in Opposition to Stipulation, those conditions are 1.4, 1.5, 1.9 and 1.17.


                                                   1
                   TESTIMONY IN OPPOSITION OF COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION
                                     DAREN K. ZIGICH
                                   CASE NO. 25-00079-UT

 1   STAFF’S OPPOSITION TO CERTAIN CONDITIONS
 2   Q.      What is Staff’s opposition to Condition 1.3?

 3   A.      Staff does not oppose the direct assignment of the Cunningham BESS costs to New Mexico

 4           on the condition that New Mexico receives 100% of the benefits. Staff does oppose the

 5           agreed-upon valuation methodology for the accredited capacity (“ACAP”) benefits of the

 6           Cunningham BESS. However, the Commission should be informed that it now appears that

 7           a direct assignment of the Plant X BESS to New Mexico may also be likely in light of a

 8           Texas PUCT’s recent Proposal for Decision1 that the Plant X BESS be approved for

 9           construction only, which would preserve the potential for SPS to directly assign all of that

10           project’s costs and benefits to SPS’s New Mexico retail ratepayers.

11

12   Q.      What is Staff’s position regarding the valuation methodology?

13   A.      Staff believes that the valuation methodology undervalues the broader benefits that energy

14           storage resources provide. Further, Staff continues to question why the ACAP, an already

15           derated capacity value should be divided further by a number greater than one (1+ the

16           seasonal PRM), especially when the PRM is not specified as being an accredited PRM or

17           a nameplate PRM. Undervaluing the benefits of the Cunningham BESS does not promote

18           the public interest of affordable rates for New Mexico ratepayers.

19

20   Q.      How does the valuation methodology undervalue energy storage?



     1
      See Texas PUCT Docket No. 58664, Southwestern Public Service Company’s Exceptions to The Proposal for
     Decision, page 63, “However, SPS proposes that if the Commission disagrees and determines that denial is
     appropriate, it should instead approve the Plant X BESS facility under the same terms as the Sandy Loam solar
     facility—in other words, approve Plant X BESS for construction only, which would preserve the potential for SPS to
     directly assign all of that project’s costs and benefits to SPS’s New Mexico retail ratepayers.”

                                                             2
              TESTIMONY IN OPPOSITION OF COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION
                                DAREN K. ZIGICH
                              CASE NO. 25-00079-UT

 1   A.   As explained by SPS in response to discovery in NMPRC Case 25-00085-UT,

 2               “A BESS can be dispatched during virtually any operational conditions including

 3               market economics, and system reliability needs while respecting transmission or

 4               deliverability limitations and charging status. SPS currently anticipates offering

 5               BESS capability into the Southwest Power Pool Integrated Marketplace in a

 6               manner consistent with the Southwest Power Pool Tariff to serve SPS and SPP

 7               needs. As a registered resource in the Southwest Power Pool, the BESS will be

 8               eligible for energy and ancillary services sales in both the Day Ahead and Real

 9               Time Balancing Market.”

10        Staff believes 1.3 of the Stipulation only recognizes the capacity benefit of the BESS

11        without taking into account the Market value of the new asset. A new energy storage asset

12        can provide more flexibility (including energy arbitrage) and Market opportunities to the

13        SPS system than its current fleet of aging steam plants and as demonstrated in Public

14        Service Company of New Mexico’s system, the energy storage resources start to supplant

15        the use of less cost-effective system resources. Therefore, the Cunningham BESS should

16        not only be allotted a capacity benefit but also an energy benefit.

17

18        Staff also opines that if the Texas PUCT is going to continue to “cherry pick” resources,

19        for example, deciding that 100% of the costs of battery storage should be allocated to SPS’s

20        New Mexico customers, then New Mexico should receive the same consideration and be

21        allowed to fully evaluate which specific equivalent capacity resources should be removed

22        from New Mexico rate base.

23

                                                    3
                  TESTIMONY IN OPPOSITION OF COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION
                                    DAREN K. ZIGICH
                                  CASE NO. 25-00079-UT

 1   Q.      In addition to testimony by other Staff regarding Staff’s opposition to Condition 1.11,

 2           what is your concern with that condition?

 3   A.      My concern is that the condition appears to be in direct contrast or conflict with the

 4           Stipulation (Section I.1.3 Condition C) approved by the Commission in NMPRC Case

 5           25-00085-UT. While Staff’s understanding of, and thus support for, the Stipulation in

 6           Case 25-00085-UT was based upon an agreement by SPS to review its cost

 7           causation/allocation methodology to better reflect the current and future system with

 8           greater penetration of variable energy and energy storage assets. Staff views Condition

 9           1.11 in this Stipulation as pulling in the other direction and, in effect, negating Condition

10           C in Case 25-00085-UT.

11

12   Q.      Can you explain the importance of Condition C in the Stipulation in Case No. 25-

13           0085-UT ?

14   A.      The 25-00085-UT Stipulation was largely supported on the premise that Condition C

15           would begin a process where SPS would review and modify its cost allocation method to

16           better align with a growing renewable energy and energy storage portfolio.2 This includes

17           reviewing customer class impacts on the SPS system over more hours than just the

18           traditional 4 peaks of the existing AED-4CP method.3

19




     2
       See Case No. 25-00085-UT, Testimony of Daren K. Zigich in Support of Unanimous Comprehensive
     Stipulation, page 6:11-20 and 7:1-18
     3
       See Case No. 25-00085-UT, Hearing Transcript of Alexander G. Trowbridge oral testimony in response to HE
     questions, page 88:10-25 and 89:1-13.

                                                          4
                     TESTIMONY IN OPPOSITION OF COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION
                                       DAREN K. ZIGICH
                                     CASE NO. 25-00079-UT

 1              In contrast the proposed 1.11 reduces the number of peak hours from four to one, as

 2              highlighted by Occidental Permian, Ltd., in its support of the Stipulation.4 This generally

 3              has the effect of favoring high-capacity factor loads to the detriment of residential and

 4              small commercial customers with more variable load factors. Further, the single

 5              coincident peak has even less relevance to the SPP’s new seasonal capacity accreditation

 6              and Planning Reserve Margin values that significantly impact resource needs and thus

 7              cost of the system. By negating Condition C from the Stipulation in Case 25-00085-UT,

 8              the Stipulation in this case does not provide sufficient public interest benefits. Therefore,

 9              the Commission should not approve 1.11 of the current Stipulation unless it is revised to

10              keep Condition C of the 25-00085-UT.


11   STAFF’S NONOPPOSITION TO CERTAIN CONDITIONS
12   Q.         Why is Staff not opposing Condition 1.4?

13   A.         SPS is retracting a request (recovery of capacity costs through the FPPCAC) that Staff

14              did not, and generally does not support. Therefore, removal of the request is not opposed

15              by Staff as further testified to by Staff witness Brossy.

16

17   Q.         Why is Staff not opposing Condition 1.5?

18   A.         Again, SPS is retracting a request (recovery of SPP deficiency payments through the

19              FPPCAC) that Staff did not support. Therefore, removal of the request is not opposed by

20              Staff as further testified to by Staff witness Mauldin.

21


     4
         See Testimony of Jonathan Ly, in Support of the Comprehensive Stipulation, page 4:16-20


                                                               5
               TESTIMONY IN OPPOSITION OF COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION
                                 DAREN K. ZIGICH
                               CASE NO. 25-00079-UT

 1   Q.   Why is Staff not opposing Condition 1.9?

 2   A.   While SPS provided some initial basis for it retaining some of the Off-System Sales

 3        Margins from Cunningham and Plant X Solar Projects, Staff is not opposed to the no

 4        retention clause in 1.9, nor is Staff opposed to SPS retaining those margins prior to

 5        commencement of cost recovery.

 6

 7   Q.   Why is Staff not opposing 1.17?

 8   A.   While Staff does not oppose the jurisdictional allocation concept in 1.17, the benefit

 9        provided to New Mexico customers is largely based on the valuation assigned to the

10        Cunningham BESS in 1.3. As detailed above, Staff does not support the resource benefit

11        (valuation) calculation in 1.3.


12   CONCLUSION
13   Q.   What is your final recommendation for the Comprehensive Stipulation?

14   A.   Staff greatly appreciates the efforts of SPS and intervenors to arrive at a comprehensive

15        Stipulation that they believe serves the public interest and has moved in that direction on

16        some issues. However, Staff finds that certain conditions of the Stipulation deserve further

17        examination and modification as testified to in all of Staff witnesses’ testimony in

18        opposition. I only discuss potential issues with 1.3 and 1.11, and other Staff present

19        concerns with other sections. Staff’s testimony as a whole seeks a Commission

20        determination of these issues, so that the resolution of this case may result in even greater

21        benefits while also addressing affordability concerns.

22

2   A.   Yes.
